questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code decides which users fall inside a percentage rollout? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A flag is enabled: true with rollout_percent 0, allow_plans ["premium"], and the caller passes plan: "premium" for a user not in allow_users. What does enabled? return?
choices: false, because a rollout of 0 percent disables the flag for everyone
true, because the plan allow-list is checked before the percentage rollout
false, because allow_plans is only consulted when rollout_percent is above 0
true, but only if the user id is also in allow_users

questions.prompt: The flag store becomes unavailable after the service has been running for hours. What does enabled? do on subsequent calls?
choices: It raises, because load_flags propagates the store error to the caller
It returns false for every flag, because @flags is cleared when a refresh fails
It keeps evaluating against the last successfully loaded flags and retries the store on every call, logging a warning each time
It keeps evaluating against the last loaded flags and does not retry until the process restarts

questions.prompt: Why is the read of @flags in lookup wrapped in @mutex.synchronize while load_flags runs outside the mutex?
choices: So that the slow store call does not block request threads that are reading flags, while swapping in the new hash stays atomic with respect to readers
So that only one thread at a time can ever call the store, preventing duplicate refreshes
Because Ruby hashes cannot be read without a lock
So that the TTL is measured only while the lock is held
